source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 38 "Statement and Decision" (questions: PDF pages 105–109, solutions: PDF page 179). tools/check_statements_decisions.ts tries every way the groups can overlap (each group has at least one member) and keeps a decision only if it is true in all of them. Q1 is corrected from B to C and Q6 from A to B. Q2, Q6 and Q7 follow the book’s Kannada where its English statements differ.

questions.prompt:
Statements:
(1) All pencils are pens.
(2) All pens are books.
Decisions:
(I) Some pencils are books.
(II) Some books are pens.
Take the statements as true. Which decisions follow?

options.C: Both decisions I and II follow
options.D: Neither decision I nor II follows

questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A decision follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: Pencils are inside pens and pens inside books, so every pencil is a book (I) and every pen is a book (II).
questions.note: The book’s key gives B (only II). But if all pencils are books, then some pencils are books too, the same reading the key uses in Q15, so both follow.

questions.prompt:
Statements:
(1) All donkeys are horses.
(2) Some horses are elephants.
Decisions:
(I) Some horses are donkeys.
(II) Some elephants are donkeys.
Take the statements as true. Which decisions follow?

options.B: Both decisions I and II follow
options.D: Neither decision I nor II follows

questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A decision follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: Every donkey is a horse, so some horses are donkeys (I). The horses that are elephants need not be donkeys (II does not follow).
questions.note: This follows the book’s Kannada. Its English reads “All horses are elephants” and “Some elephants are horses”, and then both decisions would follow.

questions.prompt:
Statements:
(1) Some mangoes are grapes.
(2) All grapes are oranges.
Decisions:
(I) Some oranges are mangoes.
(II) All grapes are mangoes.
(III) Some oranges are grapes.
Take the statements as true. Which decisions follow?

options.A: Decisions I and II follow (III does not)
options.B: Decisions I and III follow (II does not)
options.C: Decisions II and III follow (I does not)
options.D: Decisions I, II and III all follow

questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A decision follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: The mangoes that are grapes are oranges too (I). Every grape is an orange, so some oranges are grapes (III). Only some grapes are known to be mangoes (II does not follow).
questions.note: The book’s key gives A (I and II), but II does not follow; its own diagram shows I and III. This follows the book’s Kannada (“All grapes are oranges”); its English reads “Some grapes are oranges”, and then only III would follow, which is not an option.

options.C: Both decisions I and II follow
options.D: Neither decision I nor II follows

questions.working: “Some cars are jeeps” also means some jeeps are cars (I). Only the cars that are jeeps are known to be buses (II does not follow).
questions.note: This follows the book’s Kannada. Its English has “Some jeeps are buses” and, as decision II, “All grapes are buses” (a misprint); the answer is A either way.

questions.prompt:

(1) Some students are talented.
(2) Some talented people are not leaders.
(3) Some leaders are patriots.
Decisions:
(I) All leaders are talented.
(II) Some patriots are students.
(III) All talented people are patriots.
Take the statements as true. Which decisions follow?

options.A: Decisions I and II follow (III does not)
options.B: Decisions II and III follow (I does not)
options.C: Decisions I, II and III all follow
options.D: None of decisions I, II and III follows

questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A decision follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: Each statement links only some of two groups, so the groups can be drawn as a chain that touches only its neighbours: none of the three decisions has to be true.
